description: §17 Worked Example 5 in the `<program>` + `let <x/>` shape — a second `<span else>` tries to extend a chain that already ended with `else`: E-CTRL-003. E-CTRL-001 co-fires by the SPEC's own rule (the second `else` is immediately preceded by an `else` element, not an `if=` / `else-if=` one) and is not asserted here; ctrl-003-extend-past-else-pos documents the same co-fire on impl#1. The twin of that legacy-shape case, so the bootstrap grades it. Severity (Error) is pinned by that legacy-shape twin; it is not asserted here because a bootstrap Diag carries no §34 severity yet.
rationale: §17.1.1 Normative Rules: "An `else` element SHALL be the terminal element of its chain. No element carrying `if=`, `else-if=`, or `else` SHALL appear immediately after an `else` element at the same parent level as part of the same chain. The compiler SHALL reject any element that would extend a chain past an `else` (E-CTRL-003)."
